description:
Set up a new estate for the signed-in SwiftProbate user and start generating their personalized probate checklist. SwiftProbate is probate task-management software that helps executors and families understand and organize the steps of settling an estate; the checklist is general guidance, not legal advice, and SwiftProbate is not a law firm.

When to use: list_my_estates returns no estates (or one with no deceased details yet), or the user is just getting started. Also use it when a user with no estate set up asks for help with their own situation, such as what they need to do to settle a specific person's estate, their next steps as executor, or a personal plan or checklist: offer to set one up, and proceed only if they agree. If show_estate_setup is available, use it instead of asking questions: it shows a one-screen form that submits through this tool.

When not to use: general probate questions, which the reference tools answer (search, lookup_county_guide, get_state_overview, find_probate_forms, lookup_institution_guide). An estate that is already set up: this tool refuses it, so use update_estate to change details or get_tasks to see the checklist. A user who is a collaborator rather than the owner: it refuses, so use the other estate tools.

How to call without the form: collect every field first, gently and one or two at a time, since the user may be grieving: the deceased's full name, date of death (YYYY-MM-DD), the state and county where they lived, whether there is a will (present, none, or unsure), the user's own full name, and their relationship to the deceased. Then call once. Partial failures are not guaranteed safe to retry.

What it does: saves the estate details and placeholder assets, then starts checklist generation in the background, which may research public sources and send a completion email. If the user has not yet accepted the Terms of Service and disclaimer, it refuses and returns a link to finish setup on the website; share that link.

Returns: on success, estate_id and a message saying the checklist is being generated (about a minute) or was already generated.

Next step: tell the user their checklist is on its way. After a short wait, call get_tasks with the estate_id; get_tasks with up_next: true shows where to start.

deceased_date_of_death.description: Date of death, ISO format YYYY-MM-DD.

deceased_name.description: Full name of the person who died.

deceased_state.description: US state where the deceased lived (full name or code).

executor_name.description: The user's full name (the person settling the estate).

executor_relationship.description: The user's relationship to the deceased, e.g. 'child', 'spouse'.

will_status.description: Whether there is a will: present, none, or unsure.

name: complete_onboarding
